sources.title: Climbing in the Cévennes d’Ardèche
sources.notes: Regional tourism page; used for limestone cliffs, gorges and long-route character.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body: Ardèche is a southeast France outdoor region where climbing is tied to limestone cliffs, gorges and river-valley tourism.

sections.heading: History and context
warnings: No sourced history and context content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body: The legacy packet supports sport, multipitch and bouldering on limestone and granite; tourism material supports limestone cliffs and gorges.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body: The legacy packet presents Ardèche as suitable for family climbing holidays and mixed activity trips.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: The only sourced grade wording in this pass is the legacy phrase “all difficulties”, so no numeric grade range was inferred.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: The legacy packet supports spring and autumn and warns that summer is too hot for serious climbing.

sections.heading: Gear and equipment

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: The legacy packet lists Avignon, Nîmes and Lyon as nearby airport cities and recommends a car for local movement.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.body: The legacy packet lists campsites, guest houses and hotels, with reservations needed in high season.

sections.heading: Rest days
sections.body: The legacy packet mentions canyoning and canoeing as non-climbing activities in the area.
